request.statement:
Write one complete Rust program containing fn main(). Use only the Rust standard library.

Input is ASCII whitespace-separated. It begins with N S C. The next N records are:
long short kind repeat

long contains lowercase letters and hyphens, starts with a letter, and is unique. short is one unique ASCII letter, or - if absent. kind is F (no parameter), T (one text parameter), I (one signed 64-bit integer), or V (one or more signed 64-bit integers). repeat is 0 if a second occurrence is forbidden, otherwise 1.

Next are S distinct stop words. Then come C cross-option rules, in declaration order:
R k x1 ... xk: at least one listed option must be selected.
X k x1 ... xk: at most one listed option may be selected.
D x k y1 ... yk: if x is selected, every listed option must be selected.
All names reference declared long names; k>=1 and each list has distinct names.

Finally, A is followed by exactly A command-line tokens. N,S,C,A<=200000, total rule-list entries and total input length are each <=2000000. All input strings are nonempty and contain no whitespace.

Parse left to right. A stop word, the token --, or an ordinary or unknown token stops parsing and remains in the untouched suffix; no later token is examined.

A long occurrence is --long or --long=value. An attached value is forbidden for F and may not be empty. A short token is one hyphen followed by a bundle of declared short letters. Flags may continue the bundle. On reaching T, I, or V, all remaining characters are its attached first parameter and the bundle ends. Without remaining characters, its parameter comes from following tokens. If the complete token cannot be interpreted this way, it is unknown and produces no occurrences.

When a following first parameter is needed, a stop token or recognized option token causes MISSING and is not consumed. A recognized option token is a known long occurrence, regardless of attached-form validity, or a completely valid short bundle. Otherwise the token is consumed even if it starts with a hyphen. Integer syntax is [+-]?[0-9]+ and must fit i64. For V, after its first integer, consume maximal consecutive valid integer tokens, except stop words and -- always stop first.

For each occurrence, check forbidden repetition, attached-form validity, missing parameters, then conversion. Report the first parsing error:
ERR DUP long index
ERR FORM long index
ERR MISSING long index
ERR BADINT long index value
Indices are 1-based command-line token indices. Attached BADINT uses the option index.

If parsing succeeds, an option is selected iff it occurred in the parsed prefix. Check rules in declaration order. Report the first violation, where rule index is 1-based:
ERR RULE index R
ERR RULE index X p q
ERR RULE index D x y
For X, p and q are the first two selected names in listed order. For D, y is the first missing name in listed order. Parsing errors take precedence over all rules.

Otherwise print OK M R, then each occurrence in parsing order as long K followed by its K parameters, with integers in canonical decimal form. Finally print LEFT followed by all R untouched tokens. Output is compared by splitting only on ASCII whitespace bytes.
